newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Ciller warns of striking Cyprus missiles.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Ciller warns of striking Cyprus missiles.

text.p: Turkey's Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller said on Friday that Turkey would strike in the future at Greek Cyprus's missile systems if the government there went ahead with a plan to deploy them on the divided island.
"These offensive missiles will definitely not be deployed. If they are deployed we will do what is needed, if that means they need to be hit they will be hit," Ciller told a news conference.

The warning followed a similar statement by an unnamed official on Anatolian news agency on Thursday which has raised the threat of the first major military conflict on the Mediterranean island since Turkey invaded in 1974.

Turkey has accused the Cypriot government of trying to change the balance of forces on Cyprus with a deal announced last weekend to buy Russian S-300 surface-to-air missiles that could neutralise Turkish air superiority there.
Around 30,000 Turkish troops are stationed in the northern third of Cyprus, while the internationally recognised Cyprus government controls the Greek Cypriot south.

The United States has urged Nicosia to cancel the Russian missile deal and is to send an envoy to the island over the weekend to try and reduce the tension. Washington estimates the system will not be deployed for at least 16 months.
